prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished ARCHITECT COPILOT core-frame design exploration board with THREE genuinely distinct NEW character silhouettes. Reference image shows existing Copilot Base ONLY for family cues: friendly floating head, simple cyan eyes on dark face, oversized forehead goggles, no humanoid anatomy. User explicitly authorizes creativity with the CORE MODEL FRAME. Do NOT keep the reference round helmet and merely swap accessories. Redesign the head's actual architecture, massing, contour, face aperture and cheek structures radically but appealingly. All concepts are limb-free hovering head companions, no torso, neck, arms, hands, legs, feet, pedestal or humanoid robot. Keep two simple luminous cyan eyes with subtly inquisitive expressions and a recognizably paired goggle/optical treatment at brow. No mouths. Matte warm ivory primary structure, deep teal secondary casing, navy face, cyan accents, tiny warm orange functional details. No purple. No miniature buildings, floating cubes, giant compass hats or generic hard hats. Architect identity comes from structural shapes and a single small white drafting-plan icon on a side panel.

Landscape 3:2 canvas 1536x1024 or higher. Premium navy presentation board, three clean equal columns. Title 'ARCHITECT COPILOT — CORE FRAME EXPLORATION'. Each column has a LARGE excellent front three-quarter hero (about 55% board height) and ONE smaller consistent exact side profile below. No repeated 6-view panel clutter. Thin separators, ample margins, clear type. Small titles and one short description per concept as specified. Objects isolated on navy, subtle hover shadows, studio lighting, crisp economical low-poly facets, broad deliberate bevels. Every profile must match hero geometry above it.

A / KEYSTONE — 'Tapered, solid, composed'. A tall-ish inverted trapezoid floating head core with broad flat upper shoulders narrowing towards a blunt chamfered chin. Front aspect width 1.1 : height 1, NOT a sphere. Two thick ivory diagonal structural cheek pillars frame a dark trapezoid face; open face area is deep and dignified, eyes below brow. A broad flat architectural brow projects a little beyond cheeks. Two thick squared goggles are recessed into the upper third of this brow assembly, slightly angled inward, NOT separate round glasses pasted onto dome. Ivory shell taper is clearly visible from side, deep teal rear wedge, one small orange triangular inset at chin. No tall antenna. Large airy gaps only between outer diagonal cheeks and central recessed face where physically sensible, not giant holes through eyes.

B / CANTILEVER — 'Asymmetric, inventive, alert'. The widest and lowest silhouette (width 1.65 : height 1). A single bold ivory L-shaped structural outer frame: horizontal roof projects strongly to character LEFT, ONE thick upright side cheek on character RIGHT connects to lower dark teal casing. Main navy face is an offset horizontal block held under roof, with two cyan eyes; one eye slightly raised. Thin cyan reveal seam makes separation readable, no floating disconnected face. Paired rectangular drafting goggles integrated into offset brow have a wide teal bridge. One compact stepped rear counterweight on character right balances silhouette. Long roof overhang is actual geometry, not a hat. One orange end cap at roof tip; geometric side inset, no circular earphones. Angular rear/shell framing and restrained negative space make it feel ingeniously assembled.

C / VAULT — 'Open, calm, thoughtful'. The tallest and most vertical silhouette (width .85 : height 1). A chunky faceted IVORY ARCH exterior shell with flat sides, vaulted top and two thick descending cheek columns framing a rounded navy face suspended deeply between them, ending in one short deep-teal bottom crosspiece. Clearly architectural arch mass, NOT circular helmet or tall banana. The face floats visually within a structural hood but physically joined by lower crosspiece. Two wide horizontally oval goggle lenses tucked into the arch's upper brow as one paired drafting visor with central bridge; cyan eyes remain below in dark face, not inside those goggles. Rectangular side pads replace circular ear discs. One small orange keystone inset at top center of arch, no separate roof crest. Rear has broad central teal spine surrounded by ivory arch shell.

Make three clearly different and attractive believable low-poly copilot personalities, not three minor variations on the same sphere. Coherent geometry, correct eye count, no labels on model, no wireframe, no dimensions or fabricated technical statistics. All three must feel friendly, compact and readable as tower-defense support companions.
